criteria.check: Read metrics.compute and the graph draft node; every figure is computed in metrics.py and the model only receives as_table output. Deterministic, but see findings: M9/M10, M13, M3/M4 are deterministic yet wrong on probed inputs.
Read evidence lists of M1..M16. M16 lists only its numerator lines, not the inflows it is divided by.
Read graph.draft: the user prompt holds account name, period, metrics table and policy table only; no transactions.

Probed guard.check with crafted memos (probe_guard.py). Ungrounded figures pass as grounded: '40 may', '9 may', '£75 may' (date exemption), 'halved', 'a third', 'doubled', 'twice', 'one returned direct debit'.

Read graph.review/_review_problem/finalise and ReviewDecision: interrupt before finalise, reviewer required (min_length after strip), decided_at refused from caller, ungrounded approval needs override+notes.
Read categorise_one: ordered regex rules, unmatched credit returns OTHER.
Read policies/uk_sme_default.yaml and policy.validate/evaluate: thresholds, on_fail, when_missing are data; validation rejects unknown op/outcome/metric.
Read synth.py archetypes and customer names; all fictional. Did not audit every committed byte beyond src/, examples/ and evals/ statements generated by synth.
Read ingest.load_csv: missing columns, non-ISO/future dates, non-plain amounts, broken balance chain, duplicate/empty ids and extra fields all raise StatementError.
Read .github/workflows/ci.yml: pytest and evals/run_evals.py --llm fake, no secrets; ran pytest locally: 174 passed.

Swept 675 synth statements (3 archetypes x 3 profiles x months 6/9/12/18/24 x seeds 0-14) comparing M2,M5,M6,M7,M8,M11,M12,M13 to truth: 0 mismatches. synth.generate crashes for months<=4, so those statements do not exist to test.
Counterexamples found: bare 1-2 digit numbers or £ amounts followed by 'may' (or 'march') are blanked as dates; fraction/multiple words and 'one' are never flagged.

findings.claim: D4 claims owner money no longer lifts debt cover, but net operating cash flow (M9) includes every OTHER inflow, so a one-way director capital injection raises M9 and M10 and flips R2 from fail to pass with no referral (M16 stays under the 20% R9 line). The D4 test only covers a net-zero round trip.
findings.repro: 12 months of: CARD ACQUIRER SETTLEMENT +20000, DD HOLLOWAY BRIDGE FINANCE LOAN -2000, FRESHFIELD FOODS LTD DD -17500, TFR OWNER DRAWINGS -500. Before: M9 30000, M10 1.00, R2 fail. Add one 'FPS CREDIT J SMITH CAPITAL INTRODUCED' +30000: M9 60000, M10 2.25, M16 11.1, R2 pass, R9 pass (probe_inject.py).

findings.claim: The month-name date pattern matches 1-2 digit numbers followed by 'may' (and 'march'), case-insensitively, and the text is blanked before checking, so an untagged invented figure followed by the modal verb 'may' is never checked.
findings.repro: check('Total revenue was £300,000 [M2]. The account was overdrawn on 40 may be a concern.', ...) -> grounded True; same for 'These 9 may recur' and 'Arrears of £75 may follow'. Control '...overdrawn on 40 days.' -> flagged.

findings.claim: NUMBER_WORDS omits fractions and multiples (half, halved, third, quarter, double, doubled, twice, triple) and 'one' is exempt, so quantitative claims written in words pass as grounded, contrary to the D3/D6 claim that number words are read.
findings.repro: check('Total revenue was £300,000 [M2]. Revenue roughly halved and the top customer is a third of income.') -> grounded True; 'Revenue doubled, and drawings were twice the loan repayments.' -> True; 'There was one returned direct debit.' with M7=4 -> True.

findings.claim: Late VAT (M13) accepts a VAT direct debit that was returned unpaid as the quarter's payment; the reversal link (D11) is not consulted, so a bounced-then-late VAT payment reports 0 late and R5 passes.
findings.repro: Stagger 3, VAT DDs on 2025-04-07, 2025-07-07, 2025-10-07; add UNPAID DD HMRC VAT +6000 on 2025-07-09 and DD HMRC VAT -6000 on 2025-08-20. M13 = 0, R5 pass. Control with the July quarter simply paid 2025-08-20: M13 = 1, R5 refer (probe_vat.py).

findings.claim: covered_months counts a boundary month with 15+ days as a whole month, and M3's numerator includes revenue from excluded boundary months. A flat business is reported as declining and referred under R6; an anniversary statement gets M1=13 and M3 understated by 7.7%.

The Monzo importer builds descriptions from Type and Name only and never passes the payment reference (Description / Notes and #tags) as `extra`, so the invoice reference D4 requires is always dropped: every Monzo transfer in becomes OTHER, revenue from transfer-paid customers is zero and M16 absorbs it.
findings.repro: Monzo row: Faster payment, Name ACME LTD, Amount 1200, Description 'INV 1234' -> output 'FPS CREDIT ACME LTD' -> category other (probe_monzo.py).

findings.claim: Any figure tagged [Rn] that equals one of the rule's citable values is accepted wherever it appears, so an applicant figure can be stated as the threshold value.
findings.repro: With M10=0.8 and M7=4: check('... Debt service cover is 1.25x [R2] and returned direct debits were 2 [R3].') -> grounded True.

findings.claim: When --opening-balance is supplied and the export also has a Balance column, the walked balances are never compared with Monzo's, so a mistyped opening balance silently shifts M5 and M6.
findings.repro: Export with Balance 400.00, 300.00 after two -100 rows; convert(..., opening_balance=-5000) succeeds and writes balances -5100, -5200.

findings.claim: M16 is a share of all inflows but its evidence lists only the unclassified numerator lines, so the denominator cannot be traced to statement lines.
findings.repro: Read metrics.py:222-226 (denominator inflows) vs 273 (evidence=[t.id for t in unclassified]).

findings.claim: synth.generate crashes for short statements: starts[3] raises IndexError for months<=3, and rng.sample raises ValueError when fewer bounceable DDs exist than the profile needs (poor, months=4). `cma generate --months 3` fails.
findings.repro: synth.generate('cafe','good',months=3) -> IndexError; synth.generate('cafe','poor',months=4) -> ValueError: Sample larger than population.

findings.claim: The real-model workflow is gated on github.ref == main but checks out arbitrary inputs.code_ref and runs it with id-token: write, so code from any branch runs with the main-pinned Anthropic federated credential.
findings.repro: workflow_dispatch from main with code_ref=<any branch>; evals/run_evals.py from that branch executes with ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE present.
